title: The two integrals of the diagonal class
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be an integer, $A$ a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and $S$ a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Put $P=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_SP$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ be the projections and $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ the diagonal. Work in the ordinary small etale derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Here $A_T$ is the constant sheaf in degree zero and $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}A_T$, with $\mu_{N,T}(U)=\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^N=1\}$ and residue classes acting by powers, as in [def-amb-p1-trace]. Let $\delta=c_{\Delta,A}:R\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$ be the supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. For $a=1,2$, let $t_{p_a}:R(p_a)_*A_W(1)[2]\to A_P$ be the projective-line trace of [def-amb-p1-trace], and let $\alpha_a:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}R(p_a)_*R\Delta_*A_P$ be the canonical derived-composition identification from $p_a\Delta=\operatorname{id}_P$. Then both identities hold:
$$
 t_{p_a}\circ R(p_a)_*(\delta)\circ\alpha_a=\operatorname{id}_{A_P}\qquad(a=1,2).
$$
Since the etale direct image of the closed immersion $\Delta$ is exact, $R\Delta_*A_P=\Delta_*A_P$ canonically; this is the notation used in the original display. This statement uses the ordinary finite-coefficient etale twist just defined.

proof.text: The projective-space pullback formula [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] identifies $W$, over either projection, with $\mathbf P^1_P$. The projective-space properness theorem [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] makes $P\to S$ and both $p_a$ proper. In particular $P\to S$ is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $P$ Noetherian. Also $N$ remains invertible on every scheme over $S$. Thus the hypotheses defining the projective-line traces over the base $P$ are satisfied.

source.place: Proof: identify either projection with a projective-line projection; verify the hypotheses of def-amb-p1-trace

proof.text: Use the standard charts of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] over an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies each product chart with $\operatorname{Spec}(R[u]\otimes_RR[v])=\operatorname{Spec}R[u,v]$; the displayed ring identification follows directly from the polynomial universal property. On the two equal-index product charts the diagonal equation $x_0y_1-x_1y_0$ becomes $v-u$ or $u-v$ in $R[u,v]$; multiplication by either is injective by comparison of coefficients in $v$. On the two mixed-index charts it becomes $1-uv$ or $uv-1$. If $(1-uv)\sum a_j(v)u^j=0$, comparing successive powers of $u$ gives $a_0=0$ and $a_j=va_{j-1}=0$, hence every coefficient is zero. The equations define the diagonal scheme-theoretically: in equal-index charts they impose $u=v$; in mixed charts they impose $uv=1$, exactly the overlap relation. They differ by units on chart overlaps. Thus the diagonal ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and $\Delta$ is an effective Cartier divisor. Its composites with the projections are identities by the definition of the diagonal. This calculation works for arbitrary $R$, including rings with nilpotents.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences: the diagonal is an effective Cartier divisor and a section

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] to this Cartier divisor to obtain $\delta$, its compatibility with Cartier-preserving pullbacks, and the identity $\delta\circ u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. The closed immersion is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite], so [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] identifies $R\Delta_*A_P$ with $\Delta_*A_P$. The same exactness holds for module sheaves: their kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Apply the canonical derived-composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $p_a\Delta=\operatorname{id}_P$ to obtain $\alpha_a$. This fixes the source identification and the supported map without appealing to purity.

source.place: Proof, apply the supported Cartier Kummer map; make the source identification explicit

proof.text: Fix $a\in\{1,2\}$ and a geometric point $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$. The geometric fibre $F=W\times_{P,p_a}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback]. Its pulled-back diagonal $i_z:D_z\hookrightarrow F$ is the section point $D_z=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: the first coordinate is fixed for $a=1$, the second for $a=2$. In homogeneous coordinates $[b_0:b_1]$ of this point its equation on $F$ is $b_0y_1-b_1y_0$ (up to a unit sign). At least one $b_i$ is nonzero, so this is again a Cartier divisor. In the gluing convention of [def-sc-p1-standard], its local equations are $(b_0y_1-b_1y_0)/y_i$. Their ratio is $y_1/y_0$; dualizing the local generators of the ideal as in [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] gives precisely the transition relation $g_0=(y_1/y_0)^{-1}g_1$ of $\mathcal O_F(1)$. Hence $\mathcal O_F(D_z)\cong\mathcal O_F(1)$, for the point at infinity as well as for any finite point.

source.place: Proof: the fibre divisor is one rational point, with associated line bundle O(1)

proof.text:
Write $q=p_a$, $g=\bar z$, $v:F\to W$, $r:F\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and $\beta_a=Rq_*(\delta)\circ\alpha_a$. First identify the actual adjoint class before taking its fibre. The composite-adjunction unit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with the canonical composition comparison of step 3, gives $Rq_*u_\Delta\circ\eta_q=\alpha_a$, since $q\Delta=\operatorname{id}$. Put $c=\delta u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$ by step 3. Hence $\beta_a=Rq_*c\circ\eta_q$. Proper geometric-fibre exchange [cor-weil-pbc-geometric-fiber-finite] applies: $q$ is proper by step 1, $A$ is finite, and both $R\Delta_*A_P$ and $A_W(1)[2]$ are bounded below (the first is a sheaf by step 3). Use the module-category mate formula [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] for this exchange. Its naturality and the unit identity give
$$\Ex_{A_W(1)[2]}\circ g^{-1}\beta_a=Rr_*(v^{-1}c)\circ\eta_r.$$
Here the unit identity $\Ex_{q^{-1}A_P}\circ g^{-1}\eta_q=\eta_r$ follows directly from that formula: move $g^{-1}\eta_q$ through the natural unit $\eta_r$, then through the square isomorphism; the remaining inner composite is $v^{-1}(\varepsilon_{q,q^{-1}A_P}\circ q^{-1}\eta_q)=1$ by the adjunction triangle. All these maps are $A$-linear, and all inverse images of constant sheaves are identified canonically. Step 4 checks the Cartier hypothesis needed for [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], which gives $v^{-1}\delta=c_{D_z,A}$ under closed-immersion exchange. Under this same identification $v^{-1}u_\Delta=u_{D_z}$: both are the canonical restriction map of constant sheaves to the pulled-back closed subscheme, and the closed direct images are exact. Thus $v^{-1}c=c_{D_z,A}u_{D_z}=c_1(\mathcal O_F(D_z))$. By step 4 this is $c_1(\mathcal O_F(1))$. The displayed fibre map is therefore its adjoint, exactly $h_\Omega:A_\Omega\to Rr_*A_F(1)[2]$. This computes the specified supported class, including its scalar and sign.

source.place: Proof: geometric-fibre reduction of the supported morphism to the Kummer class of a point

proof.text: The ordinary finite-coefficient projective-line decomposition and trace in [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] commute with base change between Noetherian bases. Apply this with base $P$ and geometric-point base $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, both Noetherian, to identify $\bar z^{-1}t_{p_a}$ with $t_r$. By step 5, the pullback of $e_a=t_{p_a}\circ\beta_a$ is consequently $t_r\circ h_\Omega$. The definition [def-amb-p1-trace] gives $t_rh_\Omega=1_{A_\Omega}$ by the explicit calculation $\operatorname{pr}_2 b_r^{-1}b_r\iota_2=1$. Thus every geometric stalk of $e_a$ is the identity. The ordinary finite-coefficient interface is used here so that the decomposition, Kummer class, and trace have exactly the same etale twist.

source.place: Proof: projective-line decomposition and trace integrate the degree-one class to 1

proof.text: Full faithfulness of the degree-zero single-complex functor [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], applied to the abelian category of $A_P$-module sheaves, writes $e_a$ uniquely as the image of a sheaf endomorphism $f_a:A_P\to A_P$. Step 6 says that $(f_a-1)_{\bar z}=0$ for every geometric point. Let $I$ be the image of the underlying abelian-sheaf morphism $f_a-1$. Exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $I_{\bar z}=\operatorname{im}((f_a-1)_{\bar z})=0$. The map $0\to I$ is an isomorphism at every stalk, hence an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Thus $I=0$, $f_a=1$, and $e_a=1$ by the faithful degree-zero embedding. This argument works separately for $a=1$ and $a=2$. It uses stalk detection only on sheaves in degree zero; no equality criterion for arbitrary derived morphisms is needed.

source.place: Proof, final two sentences: degree-zero sheaf endomorphisms are determined by stalks

proof_origin.place: Proof, made explicit using the existing ordinary finite-etale Kummer and projective-line interfaces
